newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Many quotes, few trades on flex.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Many quotes, few trades on flex.

text.p: Flex options on individual stocks began trading Thursday and exchanges reported many requests for quotes but just a few trades.
On the American Stock Exchange (AMEX), 1,000 call contracts on Philip Morris Cos Inc traded and 600 puts on Intel Corp traded.
Also, a 400 lot in General Motors Corp and a 700 lot in International Business Machines Corp crossed, both on the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE), .
No trades in flex options were consummated at the Pacific Stock Exchange (PSE), the other exchange to offer them.
"We got some requests for quotes but no trades," said a source at the PSE. "Everybody's trying to feel their way through this thing."
Ten flex options were launched at the PSE, 15 at the AMEX and 10 at the CBOE. Three were listed on both the AMEX and the CBOE.
"I've seen what I expected, maybe a little more," said William Barclay, vice president of strategic planning and international development at the CBOE.
"People were testing kinds of requests for quotes they could put in," he said.
"Several of the markets are pretty good," he said.
He said some of the trading crowds were not familiar with some quotes because they were new and previously only available on indices.
"There was some feeling their way along as they got used to a different way of quoting," Barclay said, adding that rules clarification was the biggest question among market makers and traders.
On the AMEX, the first flex trade crossed at about 1000 CDT (1500 GMT).

The trade was 1,000 calls on Philip Morris with a 105 strike price and a January 30, 1997 expiration. The options premium was 1-1/8 and they were European style, meaning they can be exercised only at expiration.
Philip Morris shares fell 1-1/8 to 91-7/8.
The closest standard option, the January 105 call, traded 510 contracts at prices ranging from one to 5/8. That option, which expires on January 18, had open interest of about 1,730.
The only other busy Philip Morris option was the December 90 put, which traded about 1,925 contracts. Its open interest was roughly 5,970.
On the CBOE, the flex option on General Motors was an at-the-money European style put with an expiration in 1999, Barclay said.
General Motors ended unchanged at 54-1/4.
"We'll see if it turns out to be a tempest or a non-event," the source at the PSE said of individual flex options.
Flex options on selected stock indices have been available at the AMEX and CBOE since 1993.
